title: Structure and Purpose, Part 2: A Hard Question and Traps

beats.say: In part one, we learned to read the question first, and to label each sentence with a two-word job.
beats.item: Read the question; label the jobs

beats.say: We matched purpose answers by their verb, and structure answers step by step, in order.
beats.item: Verb for purpose; steps for structure

beats.say: In this video, we work through a hard sentence function question, and then the common traps.
Hard question. A sentence function question asks about the job of one sentence, in relation to the others. It doesn't ask about the purpose of the whole text.
Count the sentences carefully, label every one, and then look at the sentence the question names.

scenes.title: Read the text
scenes.text: For decades, historians assumed that a coastal town's sudden growth in the 1850s was caused by the opening of its harbor. A recent study of tax records complicates this account. The records show that the town's population had already doubled in the five years before the harbor opened, largely because a nearby lumber mill had begun hiring workers. The harbor, the study's authors suggest, may have sped up growth that was already under way.

beats.say: Sentence one is the old view. Historians assumed the harbor caused the growth.
Sentence two announces a challenge. The word complicates tells us the old view is about to be questioned.
Sentence three is the evidence. The population had already doubled before the harbor opened, because of a lumber mill.
Sentence four is the revised conclusion. The harbor may have sped up growth that was already under way.

scenes.title: What does sentence three do?
scenes.question: Which choice best describes the function of the third sentence in the overall structure of the text?

options.A: It states the long-held view that the rest of the text supports.
options.B: It provides evidence that complicates the historians' explanation.
options.C: It describes the effect the harbor had on the lumber mill.
options.D: It offers the study's final conclusion about the harbor.

beats.say: Choice A says it states the old view. The old view is sentence one, and the text doesn't support it.
Choice C says it describes the harbor's effect on the mill. The sentence says the mill drew workers, not that the harbor affected the mill.
Choice D says it's the final conclusion. The conclusion is sentence four, not sentence three.
Choice B matches our label. Sentence three gives the data that backs up the word complicates. The answer is B.
Now the traps. Each one is a way that a careful reader can still pick a wrong answer. We'll see the trap, and then the habit that avoids it.
Trap one. A purpose answer that only names the topic is a content answer. To describe tax records tells what the text is about, not what the author does.
State what the author does with the topic. Here the author uses the records to challenge an old explanation.
Trap two. A structure answer can sound right and be wrong in one step, or in the order. One bad part is enough to eliminate it.
Check the steps against your labels, in the same order. If any step is off, cross the choice out.
Trap three. If the author only explains or describes, a verb such as argue or criticize is too strong.
Match the verb to the tone. A neutral text explains, describes, or presents.
Trap four. A sentence function question is about one sentence. Students answer with the purpose of the whole text.
Answer with the job of just that sentence, in relation to its neighbors.
Trap five. For a story, a purpose answer that lists the actions is a plot answer. It says what happens, and not why the scene matters.
beats.wrong: To show Lena moving a chess piece

beats.say: For a story, say what the scene reveals about a character or a relationship.
beats.right: To show how Lena handles fear

beats.say: To recap. A purpose is what the author does, not the topic. A structure answer must match every step in order.
beats.item: Purpose is what the author does

beats.say: Match the verb to the tone, answer for only the sentence asked about, and for a story say what the scene reveals.
beats.item: Verb fits tone; one sentence; reveal
